common_name: Sharp Dressed Man Hosta (White-Centered Chartreuse-Banded Sport of Francee)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Sharp Dressed Man tolerates more sun than most hostas without melting out, though afternoon shade is still recommended in hot climates.

directions: Bred by hosta hybridizer Bob Solberg as a seedling of the classic Francee, Sharp Dressed Man forms a striking clump of very thick, triangular, dark green leaves with a dramatic creamy-white center separated from the green margin by an uneven chartreuse band. The heavy-substance foliage has a slightly rough texture and holds its coloring well even with considerable sun exposure, a trait unusual among white-centered hostas that typically scorch. Lavender flowers appear on scapes in summer. It earned the American Hosta Society's Benedict Medal for garden performance, an award recognizing hostas that perform reliably across a wide range of garden conditions nationwide.

common_name: Niagara Falls Hosta (Giant Cascading Piecrust-Edged Blue-Green Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Niagara Falls is a giant, slow-to-mature hosta and benefits from generous spacing so its cascading leaves have room to arch outward.

directions: Niagara Falls forms a large, upright clump of stiff petioles from which big, rounded, deeply veined, dark green leaves cascade outward and downward like water pouring over a ledge, giving the cultivar its name. The heavily corrugated leaves have a tightly rippled piecrust edge and arch gracefully toward the ground, creating strong textural interest even without variegation. Pale lavender flowers appear on tall scapes in midsummer. It is notably tolerant of pollution and resistant to Hosta Virus X and verticillium wilt, and won the American Hosta Society's Benedict Medal for outstanding garden performance.

common_name: Leading Lady Hosta (Giant Gold-Margined Sport of William Lachman)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Leading Lady is a giant hosta that needs several years and generous spacing to reach its full size.

directions: Registered as a giant sport of a William Lachman seedling, Leading Lady forms a semi-upright clump of heavy-substance, dark green, heart-shaped leaves edged with a rippled gold margin that matures to creamy white as the season progresses. Light lavender, tubular flowers bloom on tall scapes in midseason. Its giant stature and dramatic two-tone coloring make it an effective specimen or backdrop plant in a shaded border, and it won the American Hosta Society's Benedict Medal for garden performance, an award given only to cultivars that prove reliably vigorous and attractive across many regions of the country.

common_name: One Man's Treasure Hosta (Burgundy-Petioled Hybrid of Hosta longipes)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; One Man's Treasure is a medium-sized hosta bred from Hosta longipes f. hypoglauca and shows its best burgundy petiole color with consistent moisture.

directions: A hybrid derived from Hosta longipes f. hypoglauca, One Man's Treasure forms a medium-sized mound of very shiny, slightly rippled dark green leaves highlighted by distinctive reddish-purple spotting at the base of the petioles that extends up into the leaf bases, flower scapes, flowers, and even the seed pods. Medium lavender flowers appear on purple-streaked scapes in summer, followed by ornamental purple seed pods that persist into fall. The plant is notably resistant to verticillium wilt and attracts hummingbirds. It won the American Hosta Society's Benedict Medal for garden performance, recognizing its dependable vigor and distinctive color in gardens nationwide.

common_name: Beet Salad Hosta (Red-Petioled Hosta with Beet-Red Leaf Margin)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Beet Salad shows its beet-red petiole and leaf-margin color most intensely in cooler spring weather, fading somewhat by midsummer.

directions: Bred by hybridizer Bob Solberg, Beet Salad was considered a breakthrough introduction for red-leafed hosta breeding: it produces light green leaves held on vivid beet-red petioles, with a thin, beet-red margin about one vein wide that persists into early summer before fading to green. Rich purple flowers bloom from mid- to late summer on tall, beet-red scapes, followed by viable red seed pods. Beet Salad has been used as a breeding parent behind later red-petioled cultivars and has been recognized by the American Hosta Society for its garden performance and breeding significance.

common_name: Dark Shadows Hosta (Blue-Green Hosta with Chartreuse Margin)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Dark Shadows shows the strongest contrast between its blue-green center and chartreuse margin in cool spring weather.

directions: Introduced by hybridizer Hans Hansen, Dark Shadows forms a medium-to-large clump of large, thick, rippled leaves that emerge blue-green in the center with an uneven chartreuse-yellow margin in early spring; the contrast softens as the season progresses and the margin greens up by summer. Fragrant lavender flowers open in late spring on tall scapes. The heavy-substance foliage is notably slug resistant, and the cultivar has earned recognition from the American Hosta Society for its consistent garden performance.

common_name: Age of Gold Hosta (Giant Corrugated Gold Hosta)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in morning sun or filtered shade; Age of Gold is a giant, slow-to-mature hosta that needs several years and generous spacing to reach its full spread, and its best gold color develops with some morning sun rather than deep shade.

directions: Introduced by hybridizer Hans Hansen of Walters Gardens, Age of Gold forms a giant clump of large, round, corrugated leaves that develop increasing texture as the plant matures. In midsummer it produces near-white, tubular flowers with a faint pale lavender interior pattern on tall scapes. It is among the newest and most garden-worthy giant gold hostas introduced in recent years, recognized by the American Hosta Society for its garden performance.

common_name: Lemon Snap Hosta (Miniature Gold Hosta with Red Petioles)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Lemon Snap is a small, slow-spreading hosta well suited to containers and the front of a shaded border.

directions: Lemon Snap is a small, standout hosta grown for its bright yellow, rounded, cupped, and corrugated leaves held on upright red petioles, with red coloring creeping up the central vein of most leaves. Striped purple flowers bloom in midsummer on very dark purple scapes, attracting bees and hummingbirds. Forming a tidy, compact mound, it is well suited to containers and small shade gardens where it pairs strikingly with darker-leaved companions.

common_name: Peach Salsa Hosta (Bright Yellow Hosta with Red Petioles)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Peach Salsa holds its bright yellow leaf color best with some morning light rather than deep shade.

directions: Peach Salsa is a medium-small hosta grown for its bright, almost translucent yellow, puckered leaves paired with showy red petioles and red flower scapes, creating strong color contrast in the shade garden. It matures into a compact mound, making it a good choice for smaller borders, edging, and mixed containers where its glowing foliage color can be appreciated up close.

common_name: Leather and Lace Hosta (Blue-Green Hosta with Serrated Creamy Margin)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Leather and Lace forms a dense pinwheel-shaped clump and its cream leaf margin whitens further as the season progresses.

directions: Bred by hybridizer Don Dean from two of his earlier introductions, Leather and Lace forms a dense, pinwheel-like clump of pointed, blue-green leaves with good substance, light puckering, and a rippled, serrated, creamy-yellow margin that turns white by late summer. Fertile, light lavender flowers appear in late summer. The combination of tough, leathery blue-green centers and delicate lacy-edged margins gives the cultivar its name, and it has become a popular modern hosta across a wide hardiness range.

common_name: Choko Nishiki Hosta (On Stage - Variegated Sport of Hosta montana)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Choko Nishiki is also widely sold under the trade name On Stage and is a vigorous sport of Hosta montana.

directions: Originating in Japan as a sport of Hosta montana, Choko Nishiki (widely marketed in the United States under the trade name On Stage) forms an erect, medium-sized clump of heart-shaped, corrugated leaves with bold, creamy-white centers edged in a distinctive two-tone green margin. Lavender flowers appear on scapes in summer. As one of the older and most recognizable variegated hosta introductions still widely grown today, it remains a well-documented staple in hosta collections and reference libraries.

common_name: Inniswood Hosta (Corrugated Gold-Centered Sport of Sun Glow)

planting.note: Plant divisions in early fall or spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Inniswood is a large hosta that needs several seasons and generous spacing to reach its full spread.

directions: Discovered as a sport of Hosta Sun Glow at Inniswood Metro Gardens in Ohio, Inniswood forms a large clump of corrugated, rounded leaves with a bright gold center and a narrow, deep green margin. Lavender flowers rise on tall scapes in summer. Its combination of large scale, strong gold-and-green contrast, and dependable vigor has made it a recognized American Hosta Society award-winning selection and a mainstay in shade gardens and public plant collections.
